data.gender_notes: Sabira is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sabira is an Arabic name that is derived from the Hebrew Sabbath. In the Bible, the Sabbath is the seventh day of the week, a day set aside for rest and worship. Sabira may represent a strong, faithful woman who cherishes the Sabbath as a time of rest, reflection, and spiritual connection with God. The name Sabira carries the meaning “Girl of Sabbath” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sabira usually hope their child will grow to embody girl of sabbath and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of rest, reflection, and spiritual connection

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sabira total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_greek.name: Σαβίρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σαβίρα έχει σχέση με την ελληνική παράδοση και συνδέεται με έννοιες όπως σοφία, έξυπνη και λαμπρή. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα συνδέονται με την έννοια της σοφίας και της πνευματικής δάφνης.

in_english.name: Sabira

It carries biblical connotations of wisdom and discernment, making it significant in Christian tradition. Historically, names with similar roots were used to signify desirable qualities such as wisdom and spiritual insight.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sabira is popular in the Middle East and parts of Europe, particularly among Christian communities. It is associated with spirituality, strength, and devotion. Women named Sabira are often seen as deeply religious and upholding traditional values.
data.spiritual_significance: Sabira is believed to represent a woman who embodies the spiritual principles of the Sabbath. She cherishes this day as an opportunity to connect with God, recharge her spiritual batteries, and reflect on her faith. Her name is a constant reminder of her commitment to her religious beliefs and her dedication to seeking a closer relationship with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sabira in Arabic means "bringer of good news." In the Christian context, it represents a faithful messenger of God's love and grace. The name evokes images of joy, hope, and the promise of a better tomorrow.

historical_references.reference: Sabira, the wife of Imam Ali was called by this name. She was the daughter of Asad ibn Habib al-Ashari, the governor of Kufa. Sabira was known for her beauty, intelligence and piety. She was a great companion of Imam Ali and was deeply loved by him. Their marriage took place after the death of Imam Ali's first wife, Fatima bint Qais. Sabira was known to be a source of comfort and strength for Imam Ali during difficult times.

Saint Sabas of Palestine (Sabas the Hermit) was a renowned monk and hermit, who lived during the late 5th and early 6th centuries AD. He founded the monastery of Mar Saba in Palestine, which still exists today. Sabas was known for his extreme asceticism, as well as his miraculous powers, and was revered by both Christians and Muslims. According to legend, Sabas was once visited by the Prophet Muhammad himself, who requested his blessing.
